messages.content:
The issue seems to be related to a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` in the `HelpFormatter.findWrapPos` method. The bug report mentions that in the last `while` loop in the `findWrapPos` method, `text.length()` can be passed to `text.charAt(int)`, causing the exception. The condition in the loop on line 923 should use `<` instead of `<=`.

Here is the relevant code snippet of the `findWrapPos` method from `HelpFormatter`:

```java
923 :         while ((pos >= startPos) && ((c = text.charAt(pos)) != ' ')
924 :                 && (c != '\n') && (c != '\r'))
925 :         {
926 :             --pos;
927 :         }
```

The condition at line 923 should be modified to `pos > startPos` instead of `pos >= startPos` to prevent passing `text.length()` to `charAt(int)`.

Next, I will identify the method that needs to be fixed to address this issue.

To fix the bug and prevent the `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`, you should update the loop condition in the `findWrapPos` method. The condition at line 923 should be changed from `pos >= startPos` to `pos > startPos` to ensure that `charAt(pos)` is within the bounds of the `text` string.

Here is the method that needs to be fixed:
```java
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.findWrapPos(java.lang.String, int, int)
``` 

This modification should address the `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` in the `HelpFormatter` class.
